Case study · Invia Flights · 2025 to 2026

Three moments that decide a flight booking

Three features for an online travel agency, each answering a customer's doubt at the moment it appears. All A/B tested, all measured against conversion.

  • Conversion ↑ high single digits
  • ~1 in 3 chose the Flex Ticket
  • 3 features · 3 platforms · all A/B tested
Role
UX/UI Designer in a design team, owner of these three features end to end
Product
Invia Flights: fluege.de and other flight booking brands
Platforms
Web, iOS, Android
Method
UX KPIs, A/B tests, session recordings

Context

Customers compare the same flight everywhere. Trust decides where they book.

Invia Flights is one of the largest online travel agencies in the German market, with brands like fluege.de and airline-direct.de on web, iOS and Android.

I owned three features at three points of the funnel. Each one answers a question that used to cost us bookings.

  1. 1 · Search results Offer Box "Is this the best offer, and is the member price worth it?" Conversion uplift · still live
  2. 2 · Booking Flex Ticket "What if my plans change?" ~1 in 3 chose it · conversion ↑
  3. 3 · Payment Price Guarantee "What if the price drops after I book?" Over a third booked it

1 · Search results

The Offer Box: from a push to an honest choice

"Is this the best offer, and is the member price worth it?"

Problem. The old card had one big button that selected the member price. The normal price hid in a small text link. Customer reviews on Trustpilot and drop-offs in the booking funnel, analyzed in session recordings and analytics, showed the cost: customers felt pushed.

Tension. Making the normal price visible could cost member sign-ups, and the Product Owner was concerned about that. So before designing, we agreed on bookings as the success metric and member clicks as the guardrail.

Hypothesis. If both prices carry equal weight, customers feel less pushed and book more, even if fewer pick the member price.

My approach

I turned the card into an honest choice: two equal price buttons, side by side. I defined UX KPIs for the layout, A/B tested it against the previous card and checked real behavior in session recordings. I built the box as a modular component, so new features and layouts can be tested slot by slot without a redesign. The chip slot was planned from the start for features still to come, like the Flex Ticket in the next chapter.

Modular component

One box, four slots: top, itinerary, price actions and footer. Each slot changes on its own, so new features were added without a redesign and button layouts could be A/B tested. The tour plays one round, then it's your turn.

Result

A measurable conversion uplift, despite fewer upsell clicks. A less pushy offer sold more flights, and it is still live today. The test also surfaced ideas for the next round, ready to be tested in their own slots.

2 · Booking

The Flex Ticket: compare first, then a nudge

"What if my plans change?"

A flexible ticket lets customers cancel shortly before departure and get most of the price back. We A/B tested two layouts, iterated on the winner, then adapted it for the apps. Thanks to the chip slot in the Offer Box, the Flex Ticket also shows up right in the search results, without touching the card's design.

Result

About 1 in 3 customers chose the Flex Ticket, and conversion rose by a high single-digit percentage. People booked who would otherwise have waited.

We also aligned design system decisions with the mobile development team. Web and apps now feel more consistent, and both teams avoid duplicate work.

3 · Payment

The Price Guarantee: book now, even if the price drops later

"What if the price drops after I book?"

If the fare drops after booking, customers get part of the saving back as a voucher. We tested where in the funnel the offer belongs, then made the mechanics easy to understand.

Result

Over a third of customers kept the Price Guarantee.

What I would change next

Today the box ships pre-selected. I would make it an active choice: a guarantee customers pick themselves builds more trust, and trust is what all three features are about.

What I took away

Less push, more bookings

  • Agree on the metric firstThe PO worried about member sign-ups. Agreeing on bookings as the goal and member clicks as the guardrail settled it before the first sketch.
  • Build for the next testThe chip slot in the Offer Box let the Flex Ticket show up in search results without a redesign.
  • Test your assumptions about placementThe best moment for an offer is not always the earliest.

The variants that lost taught me the most. Happy to walk you through them.
